rationale: PINS the no-empty-endpoint rule (ONTOLOGY-WORKSTREAM definition of done: 'No unknown symbols, no empty names, no placeholder-literal edge endpoints') against a MEASURED corpus occurrence, not a hypothetical one. tree-sitter-kotlin's parse RECOVERY for `foo.bar.baz.AA.BB.<caret>CC` inserts a `type_identifier` whose text is the empty string; `collectTypeNames` read `n.text` off every type_identifier and published `references: test -> ""` at confidence 0.95 with a line number. Found by the strata census on bb_tests/repositories/kotlin@9b80c8ff (1 empty-target endpoint in the first 40 stratified files) and reproduced from the real file analysis/analysis-api/testData/components/resolver/singleByPsi/nestedTypes/ResolveTypeInTheEndOfType.kt. TWO claims are pinned, because a fix that dropped the whole recovery subtree would pass the first and be wrong: (1) NO relationship may carry an empty source or target, asserted as forbid rows per label because the shared runner reads only expectSymbols/expectRelationships/forbidSymbols/forbidRelationships/forbidDecorators and would silently ignore any other key; (2) the recovery NEIGHBOURS `caret`/`CC` and the intact `foo.bar.baz.AA.BB` chain are real identifiers the tree does contain, so their edges must survive. The per-edge pins cannot catch the defect on their own — an edge with no target matches no pin — which is why the forbid half is stated per label rather than left implicit.

expectRelationships.note: the recovery subtree is NOT dropped wholesale — `foo` is a real type_identifier either side of the broken node
`caret` is the type_projection the grammar recovered into; it is a real identifier node in the tree, so the edge is truthful even though it is not what a kotlin author meant

forbidRelationships.note: the nameless recovery node. An edge whose endpoint is "" names a symbol no file contains; R7 covers this class and the ontology workstream lists it in the definition of done.
